title: Strategic quitting: the battle traffic light for choosing which fights to walk away from
summary: Cris Pop argues that success/failure is a false binary and that quitting strategically is a real edge. He offers a red/yellow/green "battle traffic light" and a cost-benefit table to decide which fights deserve time, energy and attention, and which to drop.

principles.text: Treat failure as information, not a verdict. Stop forcing what isn't working to make space for what fits.
principles.quote: I don't believe in failure. I believe there is only information. And every time you stop forcing something that isn't working, you're making space for something more aligned with your needs.

principles.text: Stop when you hit the same wall repeatedly. Time, energy and attention are capital; don't spend it on assets that don't grow.
principles.quote: Because why spend capital (time, energy, attention) on assets that don't grow?

principles.text: The binary success-or-failure mindset keeps you stuck fighting battles that no longer matter.
principles.quote: when you're not "winning," you assume you must be "failing." So you keep fighting battles that no longer matter.

principles.text: Push wisely: too little moves nothing, too much breaks things.
principles.quote: Push too little → nothing moves. Push too much → things break. Push wisely → life opens.

principles.text: Strategic quitting is the edge: say no to almost everything so you can say yes to the rare opportunity that changes everything.
principles.quote: The real edge comes from strategic quitting. It's deliberately saying no to 99% of opportunities so you can say yes to the 1% that could change everything.

principles.text: Use a battle traffic light (red, yellow, green) to triage fights; for yellow, compare cost to benefit and move on if cost wins.
principles.quote: If you're in a yellow situation, evaluate the cost vs. the benefit with a simple table
